<break time="0.8s" /> And her hair needed better care. <break time="0.8s" /> She also told Bernice. <break time="0.8s" /> To be especially kind. <break time="0.8s" /> To the clumsy, unpopular boys. <break time="0.8s" /> Whom the other girls tried hard to avoid. <break time="0.8s" /> On the dance floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Most important of all. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a bold question. <break time="0.8s" /> That Marjorie taught her to ask at dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Do you think I ought to bob my hair. <break time="0.8s" /> In those days. <break time="0.8s" /> Bobbed hair was considered daring. <break time="0.8s" /> Even shocking. <break time="0.8s" /> So a girl. <break time="0.8s" /> Who merely talked about cutting hers. <break time="0.8s" /> Was certain to attract attention. <break time="0.8s" /> At the next dinner dance. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice tried the question. <break time="0.8s" /> On the young man beside her. <break time="0.8s" /> And to her delight. <break time="0.8s" /> He responded with eager. <break time="0.8s" /> Excited interest. <break time="0.8s" /> She promised. <break time="0.8s" /> That she would announce the date of the haircut. <break time="0.8s" /> And she invited all the boys at the table. <break time="0.8s" /> To come and watch it happen. <break time="0.8s" /> Word of the daring girl from Eau Claire. <break time="0.8s" /> Spread quickly. <break time="0.8s" /> And before the evening ended. <break time="0.8s" /> Several boys had cut in on her. <break time="0.8s" /> For the very first time. <break time="0.8s" /> Dancing in the arms of yet another partner. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice felt a thrill. <break time="0.8s" /> She had never known. <break time="0.8s" /> The dizzy pleasure. <break time="0.8s" /> Of being wanted by the crowd.
